Reachability: u1, u2, u3 and the trap u4 are all reachable (key_lost fires in real episodes, e.g. the seed-1 variant trace), and u3 is reachable via a normal successful trajectory. Coverage: every state has an else self-loop covering irrelevant or unchanging propositions (u0 absorbs non-key steps, u1 absorbs plain has_key steps, u2 absorbs key handling after the door is open — correctly not penalized since key_lost requires the door closed and nothing relocks it, u3 and u4 absorb everything else). Event/predicate discipline: only the four given propositions and else are used; key_lost is treated as a one-step event trigger, not required to persist. Soundness: state invariants hold — u1 implies has_key and door closed (the only way to lose the key with the door closed is key_lost, which exits to u4), u2 implies progress past the door; re-closing the door keeps the agent in u2 but cannot trigger at_goal, so the goal reward is only paid when at_goal actually occurs with the door open. Mutual-exclusivity constraints (key_lost vs door_open/has_key/at_goal) eliminate transition ambiguity; at_goal is impossible in u0/u1 and key_lost impossible in u0/u2. Rewards: dense monotone shaping 0.1/0.2 bounded by the 1.0 terminal reward, penalty bounded at -1.0, zeros implicit on all else self-loops including the absorbing trap, so no unbounded or conflicting reward paths. Compact: five states is minimal for ordered progress plus a violation sink; merging u3 and u4 would be wrong since one is accepting and one is dead. The u3 else self-loop is unreachable in practice because the episode ends on at_goal, but its presence is required for totality and harmless. No defects found.
